features.name: The page is a set of sections in order
features.description: The home page is built from the sections in the brief's page_plan, in its order. A section the owner switched off is not on the page.
acceptance_criteria: The page shows the sections listed in the brief, in order, and nothing else of substance.
A switched-off section is absent from the page and from the navigation.
Every section with an anchor can be reached from the navigation and the page scrolls to it.
The layout works from 360px to wide desktop screens, with content in a centred column no wider than about 1200px.
All page content is read from one typed content file (src/content/site.ts) written from the brief. There is no database, no API route and no environment variable.
verification: Load the page and check the section order against the brief.
Build with pricing and testimonials switched off and confirm neither exists in the page or the navigation.
Check the page at 360px and 1440px for horizontal scrolling.
Confirm the project has no database, ORM or API route.

features.name: Hero with main button and image placeholder
features.description: A centred headline, one supporting line, the main button, and below it a plain labelled image placeholder (aspect 16:10) that the owner replaces later.
acceptance_criteria: Headline, supporting line and button label come from the brief.
The headline and the main button are visible without scrolling at 1440 by 900 and at 375 by 667.
The hero is not full screen: the image placeholder starts just below the button.
The placeholder is a plain box with the label from the brief. No mock-up is drawn and no image is fetched or generated.
When the owner supplies an image, it replaces the box in the same frame.
Text contrast against the background is at least 4.5:1.
verification: Check the hero at both sizes.
Confirm the placeholder box is labelled and no broken image appears.

features.name: Main and secondary buttons
features.description: One main button style used in the header, hero, pricing cards and closing section, pointing to one link from the brief. An optional secondary button sits next to it in the hero only.
acceptance_criteria: With a link, every main button opens that link (a URL or a mailto).
With no link, every main button scrolls to the pricing section (the closing section when pricing is off) and the review list shows 'Set your link'.
The link is stored once in the content file and used everywhere.
An optional secondary button appears in the hero only, in a quieter style. With no link it scrolls to How it works and is flagged 'Set your link'.
There are never more than two buttons in the hero.
verification: Build with and without links and click each button on the page.

features.name: Benefits bento
features.description: A heading and a true bento grid of up to six cards of different sizes, laid out from the card count by the table in look.md. The first benefit is the large card.
acceptance_criteria: Cards come from the brief and are at most six.
The layout follows the count table: mixed sizes, no orphan card and no gap at 1440 or 375 wide.
Card titles are larger on larger cards. Every card has the same padding, and a numeral that does not overlap the title; no tinted icon squares.
Fills follow the tone (accent block, inverse block, surface) and text on each meets 4.5:1.
Each card's text is real drafted copy, not Lorem.
verification: Check the grid at both widths.

features.name: How it works
features.description: A heading and up to three numbered steps, each with a title and one line.
acceptance_criteria: Up to three steps, numbered, from the brief.
On a phone the steps stack.
verification: Check the layout at both widths.

features.name: Pricing
features.description: One card per plan (1 to 3). Prices the owner typed are shown exactly. With monthly and yearly billing, a switch shows the yearly view. The highlighted plan has an accent border and a 'Most popular' label only when marked.
acceptance_criteria: The section exists only when pricing is on in the page plan. When the owner gave no plans, two sample plans (Starter and Growth) are shown with a 'Sample' label and a 'Set your price' note.
At most three plans. Columns equal the number of plans, with no orphan card.
Yearly price = floor(monthly x 12 x (1 - discount)). Per-month equivalent = floor(yearly / 12). Calculated amounts are whole dollars, rounded down. Owner-typed prices are never changed.
Every price shown anywhere (cards, FAQ, comparison table) is read from the plan data, not typed again.
The switch changes only prices; Monthly is the default view.
Each plan button is the main button.
verification: Build with one, two and three plans and check the grid.
Compare every price on the page with the plan data.
Toggle Monthly and Yearly and compare the numbers with the formula.

features.name: Testimonials
features.description: A row of up to three visible quote cards that scrolls sideways when there are more. When the owner gave none, three placeholder cards are shown, each clearly marked as sample.
acceptance_criteria: Real quotes come only from the brief.
Placeholder quotes use the name 'Example Name', each carries a 'Sample' label that does not overlap the quote, and they are listed in placeholders.
On desktop three cards are visible at once; on a phone one card with the next peeking. With more than three, previous and next buttons scroll the row and work with the keyboard.
No logo, photo or user count is invented; initials in a circle replace photos.
One real quote is a single card at normal width, centred.
verification: Build with and without real quotes and compare.
Search the page for people or companies not in the brief other than the labelled sample.

features.name: FAQ
features.description: A heading and 3 to 6 questions in an accordion, drafted from the interview. Always on.
acceptance_criteria: Questions and answers come from the brief and are real drafted copy.
Items open and close with mouse and keyboard, and the open state is visible.
A question about price appears only when pricing is on, and quotes the same figures as the pricing section.
The FAQ has a header nav link and a footer link.
verification: Open and close each item with the keyboard.
Compare any price in the FAQ with the pricing section.

features.name: Optional sections
features.description: Examples gallery, comparison table and use-case cards, each only when switched on.
acceptance_criteria: Each exists only when on in the page plan and is placed after how it works.
Examples gallery items that need images use plain labelled placeholders.
A comparison table has at most five rows and three columns, with real drafted wording and no claims about named competitors that the owner did not give.
Use-case cards are at most four.
verification: Build with each switched on and off.

features.name: Closing call to action
features.description: One wide rounded block with a headline, a line and the main button.
acceptance_criteria: Headline and line come from the brief.
The button is the main button.
verification: Click the closing button with and without a link set.

features.name: Footer
features.description: A full footer on the surface colour with a 1px top border: name and tagline, three columns (Product, Company, Resources), a legal row with Privacy, Terms and Security, and the copyright line.
acceptance_criteria: Product links go to sections that exist on the page.
A link with no page behind it is shown, points to the top of the page, and is listed in placeholders as 'Set your link'.
No href='#' and no empty href.
No legal text, certification or compliance wording is written by the builder.
The mobile menu opens and closes with the keyboard and traps no focus.
verification: Click every header and footer link and confirm each has a target.
Open and close the mobile menu with the keyboard only.

features.name: Sample and placeholder marking
features.description: Anything that is not real yet is visibly marked and listed, so the owner knows what to review.
acceptance_criteria: Every section with status 'placeholder' shows a small muted 'Sample' label on the page.
brief.placeholders lists each placeholder with where it is and how to fix it, and AGENT_LOG.md repeats the list.
Customer logos, user counts, ratings, certifications and security claims are never generated, labelled or not.
If the brief sets demo_notice, the page shows a short notice that it is a demonstration.
verification: Search the page for logos, counts, ratings and certification words and confirm none are present.
Compare the Sample labels with the placeholders list.

features.name: Brand: tone and colour
features.description: The interview's tone and colour choices set the look, through the numbers in look.md.
acceptance_criteria: Colour 'light' and 'blue-accent' use the showcase-light mode, 'dark' uses showcase-dark. The accent is the hex in the brief.

Tone changes the design as well as the words, through the tone table in look.md: heading weight and size, card radius, how much accent is used, and motion. Bold must look noticeably bolder than calm: heavier and larger headlines, an accent block in the benefits grid and the closing section.
Text contrast is at least 4.5:1 in every mode, including text on the accent.

The accent is a background only for buttons and, in bold and playful, the large benefits card and the closing block. Icons, badges, step numbers, labels and tints never have an accent background; icon strokes, borders, numerals and text may be accent.
verification: Build with each colour choice and compute contrast.

features.name: Search and sharing basics
features.description: The page can be found and shared sensibly.
acceptance_criteria: The page has a title and description from the brief, a language attribute and Open Graph tags.
robots.txt and a sitemap with the home page exist.
verification: Fetch the home page head and check the tags.

features.name: Accessibility and performance
features.description: The page is usable with a keyboard and loads quickly.
acceptance_criteria: Focus is always visible and the page can be used with the keyboard alone.
Text contrast is at least 4.5:1 everywhere, including over images.
Images use the framework's image component with set dimensions so the page does not shift.
Motion respects the visitor's reduced-motion setting.
The page is static and has no client-side data fetching.
verification: Tab through the page.
Compute contrast for the text colours.
